The Netherlands and the German Struggle

The cabinet faces a question that reaches beyond the wording of a proclamation. Supporters of the Orange undertaking demand evidence that their sacrifices have given the nation a more commanding place in Europe. Ministers must reconcile that expectation with the rights of their partners and the power of the courts beyond the frontier. Our German policy enters the Kingdom into the contest for national leadership. Rival Great Powers may challenge our German sphere. If the Netherlands loses Great Power status and enters a German rival's sphere, that rival may incorporate the Kingdom through its national unification.

The northern sphere states join the confederation upon proclamation, while Dutch remains the primary culture and North German, Frisian and Flemish are recognised within the common state.

The Treaties of the Northern Crown

The northern union treaty has extinguished the independent authority of our former protector. Orange envoys now claim succession to its treaties and obligations. Our ministers are asked to acknowledge the common crown, while the Dutch delegation promises that a change of protector need not erase the institutions of its dependencies. Such assurances will be tested in practice: petitions once addressed to Berlin must now reach The Hague. Beyond our borders, the settlement is hailed as the foundation of northern unity. Within the council chamber, its meaning is more immediate. The relationship upon which our security rested has passed into new hands, and our government must find its place beneath the Orange crown.
Record the succession of the Orange crown.
Prussian dependency awaiting treaty succession
The Northern Victory Congress

The Prussian delegates enter beneath the banners of their conquerors. Orange ministers demand a settlement that Berlin cannot overturn by rebuilding its alliances. Invoking their dynasty's German roots and the rivers joining Dutch ports to the interior, they proclaim a northern union under a common crown. Prussia must surrender its independent diplomacy and military command. Its provinces enter the Orange state, its officials and soldiers pass into common service. Provincial traditions are promised respect, but Berlin will no longer speak as a sovereign power. German nationalists acclaim unity, while Prussian loyalists see conquest dressed in brotherhood. North Germans take their place beside Dutch, Frisian and Flemish citizens. The remaining northern courts must still be gathered before the confederation is proclaimed. The road to German unity now runs through The Hague.
Compel Prussia to enter the northern union!

The Northern Victory Congress

The defeated confederation claims already to embody northern unity. Orange ministers answer that the war has settled who shall lead it: leaving a rival federal crown intact would preserve the foundation of another coalition. The treaty compels the confederation to enter a common state beneath the Orange crown. Independent diplomacy and military command pass to The Hague, together with its provinces, officials and regiments. Delegates demand respect for provincial traditions, while Orange spokesmen promise a union connecting Dutch ports and the German interior. Supporters acclaim national strength. Opponents call it conquest dressed in federal language. North Germans join Dutch, Frisian and Flemish citizens, but the remaining northern courts must still be gathered before our confederation is proclaimed. Responsibility for northern unity now rests upon Orange.
One northern union beneath the Orange crown!

The Galician Convention

The German victory has broken Habsburg power west of Hungary. Delegates offer Galicia to Russia in return for recognition of the new order: Austria enters the German Empire, Bohemia stands apart, and the Habsburgs withdraw to Hungary. Bukovina is excluded from the offer and reserved for the Romanian principalities. Acceptance brings the Galician frontier under our authority, refusal leaves an independent Galician state between the powers.
Ratify the final act and establish the new frontiers.
The Final Act of the German Congress

The Russian court has accepted the Galician Convention. Galicia passes to Russia, whose delegates recognise the new German settlement. Austria, South Tyrol and the Littoral enter the German Empire, Bohemia regains its own government. The Habsburg court withdraws to a constitutional Hungarian kingdom, retaining the remaining crownlands and Dalmatia. Lombardy and Venetia form a protected Italian kingdom. Bukovina passes to Romania, or to Moldavia while the principalities remain divided. The signatures now turn these articles into frontiers.
